receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for circulating the Seller’s initial draft. We have reviewed it and have the following comments on behalf of the Buyer.

The Buyer is prepared to proceed on the basis of the proposed share sale structure, but the current draft is too seller-favorable and does not yet reflect the valuation and protection package required for this transaction. In particular, the Buyer proposes that the purchase price be revised to USD 38,000,000, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses, and normalized working capital as of Closing.

We also request that the Closing provision be revised to allow Closing within 45 days of signing, subject to completion of Buyer’s confirmatory due diligence, receipt of all required third-party and regulatory consents, no material adverse effect, and bring-down of the Seller’s representations at Closing.

The financial statement representation should not be knowledge-qualified. We will also need a customary suite of representations, including as to capitalization, title to the Shares, absence of undisclosed liabilities, compliance with laws, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees, intellectual property, and absence of material adverse change.

The confidentiality provision is generally acceptable, provided Buyer may disclose the terms and related information to its financing sources and their advisors, subject to customary confidentiality obligations.

Finally, please add customary indemnification provisions, including survival periods, limitations, and a purchase price holdback or escrow to support the Seller’s post-Closing obligations.

We would be pleased to review a revised draft reflecting the above.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
Counsel for the Buyer

Aldous Finch LLP
Counsel for the Seller

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, in immediately available funds by wire transfer to an account designated by the Seller, at Closing, subject to adjustment on a dollar-for-dollar basis for Closing Cash, Closing Indebtedness, unpaid Transaction Expenses, and the amount, if any, by which Closing Net Working Capital is greater than or less than the mutually agreed target net working capital amount set forth on Schedule 1. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to finalize the target net working capital amount prior to signing, based on a normalized level of working capital for the Company.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable following signing and in any event within 45 days of signing, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions expressly set forth in this Agreement, including: (a) receipt of required third-party and regulatory consents set forth on Schedule 2; (b) no law or order prohibiting the consummation of the transactions; (c) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred since signing; (d) the accuracy of the Seller’s representations and warranties at Closing, subject to materiality and Material Adverse Effect qualifications as applicable; and (e) the Buyer having completed confirmatory due diligence, provided that such condition shall be deemed satisfied unless Buyer delivers to Seller, within 20 days after signing, written notice identifying in reasonable detail a specific material issue first discovered in such confirmatory diligence that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect. Closing shall occur on such other date as the parties may agree in writing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that: (a) the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of notes in the case of unaudited statements; (b) the Company is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization; (c) the capitalization of the Company is as set forth on Schedule 3(c), and the Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company; (d) the Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of all liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws and liens that will be released at Closing; (e) except as set forth on Schedule 3(e), the Company has no material liabilities required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with the accounting principles used in preparing the financial statements, other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the most recent balance sheet; (f) the Company is, and during the applicable limitations period has been, in material compliance with applicable laws; (g) the Company has timely filed all material tax returns required to be filed and has paid all material taxes due and payable, subject to appropriate reserves; (h) Schedule 3(h) lists the Company’s material contracts, and, to the Seller’s knowledge, neither the Company nor any counterparty is in material breach of any such material contract; (i) except as set forth on Schedule 3(i), there is no material litigation pending or, to the Seller’s knowledge, threatened against the Company; (j) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment laws and has no material labor dispute pending or, to the Seller’s knowledge, threatened; (k) the Company owns or has a valid right to use the intellectual property material to the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and, to the Seller’s knowledge, the conduct of the business does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights in any material respect; and (l) since the date of the most recent balance sheet, no Material Adverse Effect has occurred.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except to its and its affiliates’ representatives, advisors, actual or prospective debt or equity financing sources and their respective advisors, or as required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, or legal process; provided that any permitted recipient is informed of the confidential nature of such information and is subject to customary confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality. Each party shall be responsible for any breach of this Section by its representatives, advisors, financing sources, and their respective advisors, except to the extent such recipients have entered into a separate confidentiality undertaking directly in favor of the other party.

5. Indemnification. From and after Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer and its affiliates and their respective representatives against losses arising out of: (a) any breach of the Seller’s representations and warranties; (b) any breach of the Seller’s covenants; and (c) fraud or willful misconduct by the Seller. The Buyer shall indemnify the Seller and its affiliates and their respective representatives against losses arising out of: (i) any breach of the Buyer’s representations and warranties; (ii) any breach of the Buyer’s covenants; and (iii) fraud or willful misconduct by the Buyer. The representations and warranties other than Fundamental Representations shall survive for 15 months following Closing; Fundamental Representations shall survive for six years following Closing; and covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms. The Seller shall not be liable for indemnification claims for breaches of non-fundamental representations and warranties unless and until aggregate losses exceed USD 425,000, in which case the Seller shall be liable only for losses in excess of such amount. The Seller’s aggregate liability for breaches of non-fundamental representations and warranties shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price. The foregoing basket and cap shall not apply to breaches of Fundamental Representations, covenants, fraud, or willful misconduct. At Closing, USD 2,125,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited with an escrow agent mutually acceptable to the parties for 15 months to secure the Seller’s indemnification obligations for non-fundamental representation claims, with any remaining balance released promptly thereafter, subject to pending claims. The parties shall negotiate in good faith a customary escrow agreement consistent with this Section.

6. Definitions. For purposes of this Agreement: “Fundamental Representations” means the representations regarding organization, authority, capitalization, title to Shares, brokers, and taxes. “Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, circumstance, effect, or development that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole; provided that Material Adverse Effect shall exclude effects arising from general economic, market, industry, regulatory, political, or geopolitical conditions, changes in law or accounting standards, acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, natural disasters, or the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, except to the extent the Company is disproportionately affected relative to similarly situated businesses in its industry.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer’s principal comments are: (1) reduce purchase price to USD 40,000,000; (2) fix the NWC target before signing and attach a schedule with objective accounting principles, sample calculation, dispute process, and true-up mechanics; (3) retain dollar-for-dollar reductions for indebtedness, unpaid transaction expenses, and NWC shortfall, with upward NWC adjustments capped or eliminated absent agreement; (4) revise confirmatory diligence condition to permit Buyer not to close for any material adverse diligence finding, not only matters rising to MAE, and extend the review period to 30 days; (5) add ordinary-course covenant, access covenant, no-leakage/no-dividend covenant, and bring-down certificate/deliverables; (6) remove or reduce knowledge/materiality qualifiers in key reps and add full reps on authority, brokers, compliance, permits, assets, environmental, privacy/data security, benefits, related-party transactions, and absence of undisclosed liabilities; (7) make the indemnity basket a tipping/first-dollar basket or reduce it materially, increase escrow to 10% of purchase price, increase non-fundamental cap to at least 20%, and extend general survival to 24 months; (8) exclude purchase-price adjustment claims, taxes, fraud, willful misconduct, covenants, and fundamental reps from basket/cap limitations; (9) clarify that fraud includes Delaware-style equitable fraud/reckless misrepresentation and is not limited by knowledge qualifiers; and (10) ensure Sections 5 and 6 are included in the operative agreement text, not merely in tracked changes.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the addition of adjustment and indemnity concepts. That said, Buyer is not yet in a position to accept the proposed economic package or the current allocation of risk.

On price, given the remaining diligence, the unresolved working-capital target, the limited scope of the proposed closing condition, and the number of representation and indemnity limitations now proposed, Buyer’s revised proposal is USD 40,000,000, subject to the closing cash, indebtedness, transaction expense, and working-capital adjustments.

We also need the following revisions before Buyer can proceed toward signing:

1. Purchase price adjustment. The target net working capital amount should be agreed and scheduled before signing, together with objective accounting principles, a sample calculation, post-closing statement process, dispute procedure, and true-up mechanics. Buyer can accept dollar-for-dollar reductions for indebtedness, unpaid transaction expenses, and NWC shortfall. Any upward NWC adjustment should be capped or separately agreed once the target is fixed.

2. Closing/diligence condition. The diligence condition should not be limited to matters that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect. Buyer should be entitled not to close if confirmatory diligence identifies a material adverse issue or material inaccuracy in the information provided. The review period should be 30 days after signing.

3. Interim covenants and deliverables. Please add ordinary-course operation covenants, restrictions on dividends/distributions, indebtedness, non-ordinary-course payments, related-party transactions, asset dispositions, employee compensation changes, and material contract amendments; continued access to books, records, management, and advisors; and customary closing deliverables, including officer certificates, lien releases, resignations as requested, and third-party consents.

4. Representations. The current reps remain too qualified. Please add customary seller authority, enforceability, no-conflicts, consents, brokers, permits, assets, environmental, employee benefits, data/privacy/security, related-party transactions, anti-corruption/sanctions, insurance, customers/suppliers, and absence of undisclosed liabilities representations. Knowledge and materiality qualifiers should be removed from key operational reps or disregarded for indemnity purposes.

5. Indemnity. The indemnity package needs to be strengthened. Buyer proposes: 24-month survival for non-fundamental reps; six years or applicable statute of limitations for fundamental reps, tax, and fraud; a first-dollar/tipping basket, or materially reduced deductible basket; non-fundamental cap of at least 20% of purchase price; and escrow of 10% of purchase price. Basket and cap should not apply to purchase-price adjustments, covenants, taxes, fundamental reps, fraud, willful misconduct, or equitable remedies. Fraud should not be limited by knowledge qualifiers or survival periods.

6. Formatting. Sections 5 and 6 appear in tracked changes only. Please incorporate them into the operative text in the next draft so that the agreement is internally complete.

If Seller can meet Buyer at USD 40,000,000 with the above protections, Buyer is prepared to work promptly to finalize the schedules and documentation.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
Counsel for the Buyer
